sequence.title: Impairment of assets and cash-generating units
objectives: Identify internal and external impairment indicators.
Calculate recoverable amount as the higher of value in use and fair value less costs of disposal.
Allocate a cash-generating unit impairment in the required order while respecting asset floors.
Explain reversal limits and the special rule for goodwill.

workedExample.scenario: A CGU has goodwill 40, plant 260 and a building 200. Its recoverable amount is 430. The building's individual fair value less costs of disposal is 190 and no separate value in use is available.
steps: Allocate remaining 30 pro rata to plant 260 and building 200: approximately 16.96 and 13.04 before floors.
Building cannot fall below 190, so only 10 is allocated to it; the remaining 20 goes to plant.
workedExample.answer: Goodwill closes at nil, building at 190 and plant at 240. The final allocation must respect the building floor; rounded preliminary allocations are not the final answer.
workedExample.auditNote: The headline calculation values below are authoritative and deliberately test floor reallocation.

practice.prompt: Asset carrying amount 180; value in use 150; fair value less costs of disposal 160. Calculate impairment.
practice.explanation: Recoverable amount is the higher amount, 160; 180 - 160 = 20.

practice.prompt: Why is goodwill tested through a CGU rather than normally on its own?
practice.answer: It does not generate cash inflows independently and must be allocated to the CGU(s) expected to benefit.
practice.explanation: Use the unit at which goodwill is monitored, within the Standard's limits.

practice.prompt: Can an impairment reversal raise an asset above the carrying amount it would have had without impairment?
practice.explanation: The reversal is capped at the no-impairment carrying amount; goodwill impairment is not reversed.

examTask.prompt: Calculate and allocate a CGU impairment including goodwill and one asset floor; explain a later reversal.
modelPoints: Apply individual asset floors and reallocate excess.
Cap reversals and never reverse goodwill impairment.

sequence.title: Inventories and biological assets
objectives: Measure inventories at the lower of cost and net realisable value.
Build cost from purchase, conversion and eligible attributable costs while excluding abnormal and storage/administrative/selling items where required.
Apply FIFO or weighted average consistently to interchangeable items and reject LIFO under IAS 2.
Distinguish biological assets, agricultural produce at harvest and inventory after harvest at a foundation level.
sections: Cost formulas and net realisable value
IAS 41 boundary: biological assets, produce at harvest and IAS 2 after harvest

workedExample.scenario: Opening 100 units at 8; purchase 200 units at 10; 180 units sold. Estimated selling price of the 120 closing units is 9.50 each, with completion and selling costs of 1.00 per unit.
steps: Under FIFO, closing units come from the 10 purchase: cost 1,200.
Weighted average cost per unit is (800 + 2,000) / 300 = 9.3333; closing cost is 1,120.
Both costs exceed total NRV of 1,020, so closing inventory is 1,020 under either formula.
workedExample.answer: Report closing inventory at 1,020. The write-down differs because the selected permitted cost formula changes cost before the lower-of-cost-and-NRV test.

practice.prompt: Purchase price 50, import duty 5, carriage 3, abnormal waste 4 and selling cost 2. What enters inventory cost before conversion costs?
practice.explanation: Price, non-recoverable duty and carriage are included; abnormal waste and selling costs are expensed.

practice.prompt: Cost 72; selling price 80; completion 6; selling costs 5. Calculate carrying amount.
What happens to agricultural produce at the point of harvest?
practice.answer: It is measured under IAS 41 at fair value less costs to sell at harvest; that amount becomes cost for subsequent IAS 2 accounting.
practice.explanation: Keep the pre-harvest biological-asset phase separate from post-harvest inventory.

examTask.prompt: Calculate closing inventory using a permitted cost formula and NRV, identify excluded costs, and explain the accounting boundary for harvested produce.
modelPoints: Calculate NRV per unit and total.
Move from IAS 41 measurement at harvest to IAS 2 afterwards.
